Welcome to Greenside Primary School
Greenside is a one-form entry primary school with a nursery at its heart, a village school in the heart of Shepherd’s Bush. Rooted in our local community and part of The Elliot Foundation Academies Trust, we work closely with partner schools to strengthen practice and ensure inclusive, high-quality education for every child.
At Greenside, we Inspire, Nurture and Challenge. We believe in strong foundations in learning and character, because kindness without ambition is not enough and challenge without care is not right. Our curriculum is ambitious, carefully sequenced and enriched through high-quality literature, the arts, music and hands-on learning.
Inclusion at Greenside is real and we live it every day. We believe in connection before correction, fairness with dignity and clear expectations. Guided by our values of Be Kind, Be Ready, Be Respectful and Be Safe, we are a calm, purposeful community where children learn to think, speak, read, write and belong.

Welcome to Greenside Primary School
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Greenside Primary School. It is a privilege to be leading a school that sits at the heart of its community and places children firmly at the centre of everything it does.
Greenside is a small school with a strong sense of purpose. As a one-form entry primary with a nursery, we know our pupils well and work hard to ensure that every child feels safe, valued and challenged. We are proud to be a village school in the heart of London, where relationships matter and belonging is built through trust, consistency and care.
The belief is simple: children thrive when expectations are high and support is strong. At Greenside, we place equal importance on learning and character. We want children to achieve well, but also to grow into kind, confident and thoughtful individuals who are ready for the next stage of their education and for life beyond school.
I am proud of the values we live by and the culture we continue to build together. Greenside is a calm, purposeful and welcoming school where children are known, supported and encouraged to be their best. I warmly invite you to be part of our community.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Greenside Primary School
Our Values and Ethos
Our Values and Ethos
At Greenside, our ethos is rooted in a clear moral purpose: every child deserves strong foundations in learning and character, and every child belongs.
We believe that education should be both ambitious and kind. Children learn best when they feel safe, respected and understood, but also when they are challenged, expected to think hard and encouraged to persevere. Kindness at Greenside is never soft, and challenge is always underpinned by care.
Our school motto, Inspire, Nurture, Challenge, captures this balance. We inspire children through a rich and ambitious curriculum that values knowledge, language and creativity. We nurture them by building strong relationships and prioritising wellbeing, ensuring that every child feels known and supported. We challenge them by holding high expectations of everyone and believing deeply in their potential.
Inclusion at Greenside is real and lived every day. It means meeting children where they are while refusing to lower expectations of what they can achieve. We adapt teaching thoughtfully, provide targeted support and work closely with families and professionals so that all children can access learning and make progress, both academically and personally.
Behaviour at Greenside is rooted in fairness, dignity and connection. We believe in connection before correction, taking time to understand behaviour and responding calmly and consistently. Clear expectations, shared language and predictable routines help create a calm, purposeful environment where children feel secure and ready to learn. Our values of Be Kind, Be Ready, Be Respectful and Be Safe guide daily life and shape how we treat one another.
Language and learning are central to our ethos. We want all children to learn to think, speak, read and write with confidence and purpose. These skills empower children to express themselves, engage with the world and succeed across the curriculum. Just as importantly, we want every child to feel that they belong at Greenside, that their voice matters and that they are an important part of our community.
Greenside is a close-knit school where relationships, trust and high expectations work together. Our ethos underpins every decision we make and every interaction we have, ensuring that children leave us not only well-prepared academically, but confident, compassionate and ready for the future.

Welcome to Greenside Primary School
Elliot's Kitchen
Elliot's Kitchen
At the Elliot Foundation, we are committed to equipping children with the knowledge, skills and behaviours necessary to succeed in life. Included within this commitment is the belief that all our children have the right to a good food education which equips them with the knowledge, skills and love of eating healthy, sustainable food that they will retain for life.
Welcome to Elliot’s Kitchen! Starting in September 2026, the Elliot Foundation is beginning the journey of bringing all of our catering in house across our London schools. Our new Executive Chef Educator, Zoé Chalton, will be working with Ms Webber and each school to develop their kitchens and incorporate them further into our Green Curriculum. This will be a phased approach starting with us at Greenside and Griffin Primary. The Trust will be using our school, which has operated a very successful in-house kitchen, as a model for excellence and we’ll be supported by our new partnership with Chefs in Schools. Through this approach we will be making lunch a real part of the learning experience. All our lunches will be in line with the new school food standards, reflect the seasons and be made from scratch by well-trained staff using the freshest ingredients from suppliers who support our mission.
Our Chef Jo and her team, alongside Zoe, will continue to cook delicious vegetarian lunches that are served in our Greenside lunchroom. Jo is a passionate cook who has worked in a variety of different food environments around the world. The lunches offer a choice of two hot vegetarian meals with salad, bread and a pudding. There is a greater emphasis on the communal aspect of eating, with more food being served at the table and the pupils are encouraged to serve each other. We are pleased to say that we are now a 100% school lunch community – we do not allow packed lunches at all here at Greenside. The philosophy behind our move to vegetarian food is that we can provide an educational experience, showing the importance of sustainability, introducing the pupils to alternatives, as well as giving them a fully inclusive dining experience. Our Greenside garden continues to thrive and, thanks to the help of our pupils and family volunteers, we are able to supply the kitchen with fresh vegetables throughout the year. We have been featured on Jamie’s Meat Free Meals – this was a great way to celebrate the success of our Food Experience.
Nut Allergies Greenside has pupils with serious peanut allergies. We do not serve nuts at school. Please be aware that because of this we cannot allow peanut or peanut related foods at Greenside in any capacity. This includes: Cereal bars with nuts Peanut butter Packets or peanuts of other nuts Biscuits that might be contaminated by nuts and have a warning on their labels Cakes with added nuts Satays of any description

Welcome to Greenside Primary School
Learning
Curriculum
Curriculum at Greenside At Greenside, our curriculum is built on the foundation of the National Curriculum, with a distinctive twist that reflects our unique identity and values. While we deliver all statutory subjects with academic rigour, our approach goes far beyond compliance. We offer a rich, integrated learning experience designed to inspire curiosity, nurture individuality, and develop well-rounded, future-ready learners.
Inspiration Through Innovation We believe that learning should be dynamic, meaningful and joyful. Our curriculum is driven by three core elements: food, film and fun. These are not add-ons; they are essential ingredients in how we engage children in deep learning, personal growth and creative expression. Through a diverse range of texts, cinematic experiences, hands-on projects and community engagement, our pupils develop confidence, independence and resilience.
The Green Curriculum at the Heart Sustainability is embedded across our curriculum, not just as a subject but as a way of thinking and living. Our Green Curriculum empowers children to care for the planet, make environmentally conscious choices and understand their role as global citizens. Whether growing food in our school garden, learning outdoors or reducing waste through school initiatives, pupils develop environmental literacy and take real action to make a difference.
We promote learning experiences linked to food, nature and outdoor exploration in all areas of the curriculum. Sustainability isn’t an isolated topic; it is a mindset woven into everything we do.
English Through Power of Reading Our English curriculum is enriched by a deep engagement with literature. We use high-quality texts to spark imagination, build vocabulary and encourage critical thinking. This interdisciplinary approach helps pupils to explore different perspectives, develop empathy and express their ideas with clarity and creativity, both in writing and through oracy.
Our use of technology prepares children for the digital world while promoting creativity, responsibility and adaptability.
A Balanced Curriculum We take a combined approach to curriculum design, drawing on a range of carefully chosen schemes and pedagogical approaches to support, deepen and enrich learning. These do not lead our curriculum but are used thoughtfully to support high-quality planning and delivery. All curriculum decisions are made with our cohort and demographic in mind, ensuring that content is relevant, inclusive and responsive to the needs of our pupils.
Throughout their time at Greenside, children take part in real-world projects, creative exhibitions and community events. Whether baking bread with our kitchen team, performing music or solving local environmental challenges, our pupils are active, curious participants in their own learning journey.
For more information about our curriculum, please contact the Head of School.
